attr.fort.name: Chittorgarh Fort
attr.fort.desc: A UNESCO World Heritage Site and the largest fort in India. A symbol of resilience and architectural brilliance.
attr.padmini.name: Padmini Palace
attr.padmini.desc: A remarkably elegant three-story structure surrounded by a serene lotus pool. The palace represents the grace and beauty of the legendary Queen Padmini and the bravery of the women of Mewar.
attr.bassi.name: Bassi Sanctuary
attr.bassi.desc: Explore the Vindhyan wilderness, home to historic hunting towers, leopards, and the graceful Sarus Crane.
attr.temple.name: Saawariya ji Temple
attr.temple.desc: Dedicated to Lord Krishna, this temple is a significant pilgrimage site known for its grandeur.
attr.vijay.name: Vijay Stambh
attr.vijay.desc: Built by Maharana Kumbha between 1440 AD and 1448 AD to immortalise his triumph of defeating the rulers of Malwa and Gujarat.
attr.kirti.name: Kirti Stambha (Tower of Fame)
attr.kirti.desc: A masterpiece of medieval architecture dedicated to Adinath, the first Jain Tirthankara. The tower stands as a symbol of spiritual heritage and artistic prosperity.
attr.kalika.name: Kalika Mata Temple
attr.kalika.desc: An 8th-century temple originally built for the Sun God, later rededicated to Goddess Kali by Rana Hameer in the 14th century.
kalika.hero.title: Kalika Mata Temple
kalika.hero.desc: An 8th-century sun temple transformed into a powerful shrine of Goddess Kali.
kalika.overview.p1: Built in 8th century AD, this ancient structure was initially constructed to worship the sun god.
kalika.overview.p2: In the 14th century, Rana Hameer rebuilt it and then temple was dedicated to Goddess Kali, the symbol of power and valour.
kalika.visuals.exterior.title: Temple Architecture
kalika.visuals.exterior.desc: The majestic exterior of the 8th-century temple, showcasing its grand shikhara and ancient stones.
kalika.visuals.idols.title: Goddess Kalika
kalika.visuals.idols.desc: The powerful shrine of Goddess Kali, the presiding deity of power and protection for the Mewar royals.
kalika.references.title: References
attr.kalika_arch.facade.name: Exterior Friezes
attr.kalika_arch.facade.desc: The outer walls are decorated with rows of sculptures, though weathered by time, they still reveal the artistic excellence.
attr.jain.name: Jain Temples
attr.jain.desc: A group of 27 ancient Jain temples showcasing intricate carvings and spiritual serenity.
attr.gaumukh.name: Gaumukh Reservoir
attr.gaumukh.desc: Known as the 'Mouth of the Cow,' this sacred water body is fed by a perennial spring that flows through a beautifully carved stone mouth of a cow. It was the primary source of water for the fort during its many historic sieges, earning Chittorgarh the reputation of being a 'Water Fort.' Pilgrims and tourists alike visit the reservoir to witness the holy spring and feed the hundreds of fish that consider this water their home. Located at the edge of a cliff, the site offers a tranquil escape with the sound of trickling water providing a peaceful backdrop. It is considered one of the most auspicious spots in the fort, reflecting the deep connection between heritage and nature.
attr.fateh.name: Fateh Prakash Palace
attr.fateh.desc: Constructed by Maharana Fateh Singh as his residence, now a museum showcasing wood crafts, weapons, and historic artifacts.
attr.menal.name: Menal Waterfall
attr.menal.desc: A beautiful 150-meter waterfall situated in a deep V-shaped valley.
attr.meera.name: Meera Bai Temple
attr.meera.desc: A symbol of pure devotion, this temple is dedicated to the mystic poet-saint Meera Bai. Built in the classic Rajput style by Maharana Kumbha, it features a pavilion where Meera Bai composed her bhajans.
attr.ratan.name: Ratan Singh Palace
attr.ratan.desc: Overlooking the Ratneshwar Talab, this palace offers a glimpse into the royal lifestyle of the Mewar rulers.
attr.sanwaliya.name: Sanwaliya ji Temple
attr.sanwaliya.desc: A grand temple dedicated to Lord Krishna, where millions of devotees visit every year. Established after the miraculous discovery of three idols in 1840.
attr.kumbha_palace.name: Rana Kumbha Palace
attr.kumbha_palace.desc: One of the most massive and historic structures in the fort, this palace was the residence of Maharana Kumbha. It is steeped in legend and serves as a powerful reminder of the fort's prime.
attr.kumbha_shyam.name: Kumbha Shyam Temple
attr.kumbha_shyam.desc: Built in the 8th century, this temple features unique intricate architecture of the Rajput style.
attr.light.name: Light & Sound Show
attr.light.desc: A mesmerizing evening show narrating the history of Chittorgarh Fort.
chron.hero.title: The Mewar Chronicles
chron.hero.sub: Legends of Sacrifice, Valour, and Devotion
legend.padmini.title: Rani Padmini
legend.padmini.subtitle: The Saga of Grace and Sacrifice
legend.padmini.desc: Known for her ethereal beauty and sharp intellect, Rani Padmini is a symbol of supreme sacrifice. To protect the honour of Chittorgarh from the siege of Alauddin Khalji, she led the heroic 'Jauhar' along with thousands of brave women, a tale that still echoes in the fort's wind.
legend.pratap.title: Maharana Pratap
legend.pratap.subtitle: The Unyielding Spirit
legend.pratap.desc: The lion of Mewar who never bowed to the Mughal Empire. Along with his legendary horse Chetak, he fought for the freedom of his land in the battle of Haldighati. His life was a testament to the belief that liberty is worth more than a golden throne.
legend.panna.title: Panna Dhai
legend.panna.subtitle: The Ultimate Sacrifice
legend.panna.desc: A nursemaid like no other, who sacrificed her own son, Chandan, to save the infant Prince Udai Singh from an assassin. Her unwavering loyalty ensured the continuation of the Mewar dynasty, proving that some bonds are deeper than blood.
legend.meera.title: Meera Bai
legend.meera.subtitle: The Devotion of the Soul
legend.meera.desc: A princess who renounced royal luxuries for the love of Lord Krishna. Her soulful bhajans and fearless devotion redefined spirituality, reminding the world that the greatest strength lies in pure, unshakeable love.

fact.title: Did You Know?
fact.1: Chittorgarh Fort is the largest fort complex in India and Asia, sprawling over 700 acres.
fact.2: The fort originally had 84 water bodies, including ponds, wells, and stepwells.
fact.3: Vijay Stambh (Tower of Victory) features 157 narrow steps to reach the 9th floor.
fact.4: The fort was recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2013 for its architectural grandeur.
fact.5: Meera Bai, the legendary poet-saint and devotee of Lord Krishna, resided within these fort walls.
fact.6: The fort's history dates back to the 7th century, originally built by the Maurya Dynasty.
fact.7: There are 7 massive gateways (Pols) to enter the citadel, each with its own historical significance.
fact.8: Rani Padmini's Palace is uniquely built amidst a beautiful lotus pool.
fact.9: Kirti Stambh (Tower of Fame) is a 12th-century tower dedicated to the first Jain Tirthankara, Adinath.
fact.10: The Gaumukh Reservoir is a sacred water body fed by a spring that flows from a carved cow's mouth.

plan.1.title: 1 Day: The Royal Heritage Tour (Premium)
plan.1.desc: A meticulously curated journey through 1300 years of valor. Experience the grandeur of the largest fort in India with deep historical immersion.
plan.1.sch.0.title: Arrival & The Seven Gates
plan.1.sch.0.activity: Begin your ascent driving through the seven historic pols (gates): Padan, Bhairon, Hanuman, Ganesh, Jodla, Laxman, and finally the main Ram Pol. Tip: Stop at the memorial chhatris of Jaimal and Patta between Bhairon and Hanuman Pol to pay respects to the martyrs of the 1568 siege.
plan.1.sch.1.title: Rana Kumbha Palace & Museums
plan.1.sch.1.activity: Explore the ruins of the grandest palace in the fort. Visit the Government Museum inside Fateh Prakash Palace to see ancient sculptures, medieval weaponry, and royal artifacts. Legend says Rani Padmini performed Jauhar in the cellars of Rana Kumbha Palace.
plan.1.sch.2.title: Towers of Victory & Fame
plan.1.sch.2.activity: Marvel at the Vijay Stambha (Tower of Victory), a 9-story marvel carved with thousands of Hindu deities. Pro Tip: The best view of the fort is from the top floor. Nearby, visit the Kirti Stambha (Tower of Fame), a 12th-century Jain monument dedicated to Adinath.
plan.1.sch.3.title: Temples of Devotion
plan.1.sch.3.activity: Visit the Kumbha Shyam Temple (Varaha avatar of Vishnu) and the Meera Bai Temple. Sit for a moment where the poet-saint Meera Bai once sang bhajans for Lord Krishna. The intricate carvings here are a photographer's delight.
plan.1.sch.4.title: Royal Rajasthani Feast
plan.1.sch.4.activity: Head to 'Hotel Pratap Palace' or nearby local eateries for an authentic thali featuring Dal Baati Churma, Gatte ki Sabzi, and Bajre ki Roti. Experience the hospitality of Mewar.
plan.1.sch.5.title: Rani Padmini's Palace
plan.1.sch.5.activity: Visit the summer pavilion of Queen Padmini, surrounded by a lotus pool. This is the legendary spot where Alauddin Khilji is said to have glimpsed her reflection. The gardens here are lush and perfect for a leisurely walk.
plan.1.sch.6.title: Gaumukh Reservoir & Kalika Mata
plan.1.sch.6.activity: Walk down to the Gaumukh Reservoir, fed by a perennial spring from a carved cow's mouth. Then, visit the 7th-century Kalika Mata Temple (originally a Sun temple), devoted to Goddess Kalika, a form of Durga, to witness the sunset prayer.
plan.1.sch.7.title: Sound & Light Show
plan.1.sch.7.activity: Conclude with the spectacular Sound & Light show (English/Hindi) at the fort complex. Watch the history of Chittorgarh come alive through lights projected on the ancient walls. (Ticket: Approx ₹100, varying by season).
plan.2.title: 2 Days: Wildlife & Waterfalls Expedition
plan.2.desc: Beyond the fort lies the untamed beauty of the Aravallis. Discover leopards in the wild and ancient temples hidden by waterfalls.
plan.2.sch.0.title: Complete Heritage Tour
plan.2.sch.0.activity: Follow the comprehensive 1-Day Itinerary detailed above for a full immersion into the fort's history.
plan.2.sch.1.title: Sunrise Drive to Bassi
plan.2.sch.1.activity: Depart early for Bassi Wildlife Sanctuary (25km). The morning mist over the Aravalli hills offers stunning photographic opportunities.
plan.2.sch.2.activity: Board a Gypsy for a safari. Keep your eyes peeled for Sloth Bears, Hyenas, and the Four-horned Antelope. The sanctuary is also a birdwatcher's paradise (Peacocks, Eagles, Hawkes).
plan.2.sch.3.title: Bassi & Orai Dams
plan.2.sch.3.activity: Visit the Bassi Dam and Orai Dam. The stillness of the water against the rugged hills is mesmerizing. Perfect for a mid-morning break and nature photography.
plan.2.sch.4.title: Picnic at Menal
plan.2.sch.4.activity: Drive to Menal (approx 60km). Enjoy a picnic lunch near the gorge. The area is lush green, especially post-monsoon.
plan.2.sch.5.title: Menal: The Waterfall & Temple Complex
plan.2.sch.5.activity: Explore the Mahanaleshwar Temple complex (11th Century). Witness the Menal River plunging 150 feet into a gorge—a breathtaking sight during the monsoon.
plan.2.sch.6.title: Rural Drive Back
plan.2.sch.6.activity: Return to Chittorgarh via the scenic rural route. Witness local village life, cattle herders, and traditional mud houses.
plan.2.sch.7.title: Dinner at Castle Bijaipur
plan.2.sch.7.activity: Optional: drive to Castle Bijaipur (heritage hotel) for a royal dinner experience, or enjoy local street food (Mirchi Vada, Pyaaz Kachori) in Chittorgarh market.
plan.3.title: 3 Days: The Soul of Mewar
plan.3.desc: A holistic journey covering History, Nature, Divinity, and Art. Meet the artisans of Akola and seek blessings at Saawariya ji Seth.
plan.3.sch.0.title: History & Nature
plan.3.sch.0.activity: Complete the 2-Day Itinerary covering the Fort, Bassi Sanctuary, and Menal Waterfalls.
plan.3.sch.1.title: Pilgrimage to Mandraphiya
plan.3.sch.1.activity: Drive 40km to the Saawariya ji Seth Temple. Dedicated to Lord Krishna, this temple is famous for its opulence and the belief that the Lord is a business partner to his devotees.
plan.3.sch.2.title: Akola: The Indigo Village
plan.3.sch.2.activity: Visit Akola (Chhipon-ka-Akola). Watch the master craftsmen perform 'Dabu' printing—a unique mud-resist technique. See the indigo dyeing pits that have been used for generations.
plan.3.sch.3.title: Traditional Village Lunch
plan.3.sch.3.activity: Experience hospitality in a rural home or a local eatery. Try 'Makki ki Raab' (Corn soup) and fresh buttermilk.
plan.3.sch.4.title: Artisan Shopping
plan.3.sch.4.activity: Purchase fabrics directly from the source. Akola prints are famous for not bleeding color. Pick up bedsheets, sarees, and dress materials at unbeatable prices.
plan.3.sch.5.title: Local Market Exploration
plan.3.sch.5.activity: Return to Chittorgarh city. Explore Sadar Bazaar and Station Road. Look for 'Thewa' jewelry (gold on glass), wooden toys from Bassi, and colorful Jutits (shoes).
plan.3.sch.6.title: Royal Farewell
plan.3.sch.6.activity: Conclude your trip with a rooftop dinner overlooking the illuminated Fort. Reflect on 1300 years of history, the roar of the wild, and the color of indigo.

faq.title: People Also Ask about Chittorgarh
faq.a1: Chittorgarh is world-famous for the Chittorgarh Fort, the largest fort in India and a UNESCO World Heritage site. It is renowned for its magnificent Rajputana architecture, the legendary story of Rani Padmini's Jauhar, and being the land of devotion for the poetess-saint Meera Bai and the bravery of Maharana Pratap.
faq.q2: Which is the best month to visit Chittorgarh?
faq.a2: The best time to visit Chittorgarh is between October and March. During these winter months, the weather is pleasant and ideal for exploring the massive fort complex on foot. Visiting during the monsoon (July to September) is also beautiful as the landscape turns lush green.
faq.q3: How many days are enough for Chittorgarh?
faq.a3: A 1 to 2 day itinerary is sufficient to explore Chittorgarh. You need at least one full day to see the main attractions inside the fort like Vijay Stambha, Kirti Stambha, Rana Kumbha Palace, and Padmini Palace. A second day allows you to visit nearby attractions like the Bassi Wildlife Sanctuary or Menal Waterfalls.
faq.a4: Yes, Chittorgarh is absolutely worth visiting for history buffs, architecture lovers, and anyone interested in Rajput heritage. Simply walking through its massive 700-acre fort complex, observing the detailed carvings on the Towers of Victory and Fame, and feeling the echoes of legendary heroic tales makes it a must-visit destination in Rajasthan.

fort.hero.title: Chittorgarh Fort
fort.hero.desc: The largest fort in India and a UNESCO World Heritage site, resonating with stories of courage, sacrifice, and the immortal spirit of Rajputana.
fort.section.monuments.title: Valor Etched in Stone: Majestic Monuments
fort.overview.p1: Spread across 700 acres atop a high hill, Chittorgarh Fort is the epitome of Rajput spirit. It has stood through three major sieges, each time witnessing unparalleled valor.
fort.overview.p2: Known as the 'Water Fort', it houses 84 water bodies, ensuring it could withstand long sieges. Today, its majestic ruins tell the sagas of Rani Padmini and Maharana Pratap.
fort.history.era1.title: The Genesis of Glory
fort.history.era1.desc: Rising from the Aravalli peaks, the citadel was founded by the Maurya dynasty, eventually becoming the eternal seat of Mewar’s sovereignty and a beacon of Rajputana pride.
fort.history.era2.title: Chronicles of Immortality
fort.history.era2.desc: The fortress stood as an unyielding titan against the tides of various empires. Each siege was met with the thunder of swords and the sacred flame of courage, where sacrifice defined the very soul of the land.
fort.history.era3.title: The Eternal Vigil
fort.history.era3.desc: Now a UNESCO World Heritage treasure, the slumbering stones of Chittorgarh continue to whisper the sagas of immortal kings and defiant queens, standing as India’s ultimate symbol of resilience.
fort.tracker.title: Golden Hour Tracker
fort.tracker.tip: Soft, warm lighting perfect for architectural photography.
vijay.hero.title: Vijay Stambh
vijay.history.p1: Vijay Stambh (the Tower of Victory) was built by Maharana Kumbha between 1440 AD and 1448 AD to immortalise his triumph of defeating the rulers of Malwa and Gujarat.
vijay.architecture.p1: Built partly from red sandstone and partly white marble, this architectural wonder is nine-storey tower decorated with detailed sculptures of Hindu gods and goddesses.
vijay.experience.p1: Narrow steps lead to the terrace where one can catch a spectacular view of the entire town from the balconies.
vijay.references.title: References
padmini.hero.title: Padmini Palace
padmini.hero.desc: Surrounded by a serene lotus pool, this elegant structure is the site of the legendary mirror glimpse that sparked the siege of 1303.
padmini.overview.p1: Padmini Palace is a remarkably elegant three-story structure situated within the southern part of Chittorgarh Fort. It is uniquely surrounded by a lotus pool, which served as a natural cooling system and a beautiful aesthetic feature.
padmini.overview.p2: The palace is inextricably linked to the legend of Rani Padmini, whose beauty and bravery are celebrated in the poem 'Padmavat'. It stands as a symbol of the courage of Mewar's women.
padmini.history.era1.title: A Royal Retreat
padmini.history.era1.desc: Constructed as a summer retreat for the royal family, the palace was designed to be a peaceful sanctuary away from the main administrative buildings.
padmini.history.era2.title: The Mirror Legend
padmini.history.era2.desc: According to legend, this is where Alauddin Khilji saw Padmini's reflection in a mirror, leading to the conflict that changed the course of Mewar's history.
padmini.history.era3.title: A Silent Witness
padmini.history.era3.desc: Today, the palace remains one of the most visited spots in the fort, offering a tranquil space for reflection on the fort's tragic yet heroic past.
attr.padmini_arch.pool.name: The Lotus Pool
attr.padmini_arch.pool.desc: The palace is surrounded by a large water body, which originally bloomed with lotuses, providing a stunning visual and temperature regulation.
attr.padmini_arch.pavilion.name: Summer Pavilion
attr.padmini_arch.pavilion.desc: The central pavilion is built in the middle of the water, accessible only by a bridge, ensuring privacy and security for the royal ladies.
attr.padmini_arch.zenana.name: Zenana Mahal
attr.padmini_arch.zenana.desc: The inner apartments featured delicate stone screens (jalis) that allowed the queens to view the outside world without being seen.
kumbha.hero.title: Rana Kumbha Palace
kumbha.hero.desc: A ruined edifice of great historical and architectural interest, representing the heart of Mewar's royal legacy.
kumbha.history.p1: A ruined edifice of great historical and architectural interest, this is one of the most massive monuments in the Fort of Chittor. Due to the restoration of this ancient palace by Maharana Kumbha, it is known as Kumbha Mahal. The original palace predates Kumbha.
kumbha.layout.p1: The main entrance to the palace is the Tripolia Darwaza, which is currently closed. The open area in front of the Tripolia door is called Darikhana. On the right side of the Darikhana are situated the Suraj Gokhada and the main palace and on the left side are the Janana Mahal and Kanwarpada’s palaces.
kumbha.cellars.p1: There are many dungeons under the palaces which may have been due to the construction of new palaces above the chambers of the earlier palace. Many historians have expressed the estimate of Jauhar in these cellars.
kumbha.references.title: References
attr.kumbha_arch.cellars.name: The Underground Vaults
attr.kumbha_arch.cellars.desc: The palace contains a series of dark, interconnected underground chambers believed to be the site of historic Jauhars and secret royal passages.
gaumukh.hero.title: Gaumukh Reservoir
gaumukh.hero.desc: A perennial spring that flows through a rock shaped like a cow's mouth, serving as the fort's main water source for centuries.
gaumukh.overview.p1: Gaumukh Reservoir is a deep tank filled by a perennial spring that flows from a rock shaped like a cow's mouth (Gau-mukh). It is situated at the edge of the fort and has been a vital source of water for the residents and soldiers for over a thousand years.
gaumukh.overview.p2: The site is considered holy by devotees who perform rituals and take dips in the sacred water. The surrounding area is dotted with small temples and carvings, creating a serene and spiritual atmosphere.
gaumukh.history.era1.title: The First Spring
gaumukh.history.era1.desc: Since the fort's earliest days, Gaumukh has been the most important water source. Its location near the Samadhiswar Temple makes it a focal point of religious activity.
gaumukh.history.era2.title: The Siege Life-line
gaumukh.history.era2.desc: During legendary sieges, the reservoir's hidden springs provided cool, fresh water to thousands of defenders, allowing the fort to hold out for months against invaders.
gaumukh.history.era3.title: A Pilgrim's Haven
gaumukh.history.era3.desc: Today, Gaumukh is a must-visit spot for both its natural beauty and spiritual significance. The sight of the water cascading into the deep green pool remains one of the fort's most iconic views.
attr.gaumukh_arch.rock.name: The 'Gaumukh' Spout
attr.gaumukh_arch.rock.desc: The spring water emerges from a natural rock formation meticulously carved into the shape of a cow's head, representing the sacred river Ganga.
attr.gaumukh_arch.temple.name: Temple Cluster
attr.gaumukh_arch.temple.desc: The reservoir is surrounded by small, ancient niches and shrines dedicated to various Hindu deities, showing the religious importance of water in Rajput culture.
attr.gaumukh_arch.steps.name: The Ghats
attr.gaumukh_arch.steps.desc: Stone steps lead down to the water level, designed to allow pilgrims to reach the reservoir safely even as water levels fluctuate throughout the seasons.
fateh.hero.title: Fateh Prakash Palace
fateh.history.p1: Constructed by Maharana Fateh Singh, this palace functioned as his residence. It was built in the Rajput style of architecture as a declaration of his taste for art and culture. It has now been converted into a museum.
fateh.collection.p1: The palace has a vast collection of wood crafts of Bassi village, post medieval statues of Jain Ambica and Indra from Rashmi village, weapons such as axes, knives and ancient shields, clay replicas of regional tribal people clad in their traditional costumes, paintings, and crystal ware.
fateh.info.p1: Timings: 09:45 am to 04:45 pm. Entry fee: Indian Rs. 20 (Child Rs 10), Foreigner Rs. 100 (Child Rs 50).
fateh.references.title: References
kumbha_shyam.hero.title: Kumbha Shyam Temple
kumbha_shyam.hero.desc: An 8th-century marvel dedicated to Lord Varaha, standing as a testament to Mewar's spiritual heritage.
kumbha_shyam.history.p1: Kumbha Shyam Temple was built in the 8th century. Originally this temple was dedicated to Lord Varaha (boar). Maharana Kumbha later renovated this temple and the idol of Kumbhashyam was installed here.
kumbha_shyam.architecture.p1: Built in Indo-Aryan style is a wonderful example of architectural craft.
jain.hero.title: Jain Temples
jain.hero.desc: Sacred sanctuaries of peace and intricate artistry within the fort walls.
jain.overview.p1: The fort of Chittor has six Jain temples contained within its walls. The largest among them is the temple of Bhagawan Adinatha which has 52 ‘devkulikas’.
jain.satbees.p1: Satbees Deori Jain Temple is situated on the right side in front of Badi Pol in Chittorgarh Fort. Probably because of the total 27 deities built in the temple, it is called the satbees deori temple.
jain.architecture.p1: The craftsmanship done on the inside and outside in these temples is amazing. There are two more temples on the back side of the main temple.
jain.references.title: References
meera.hero.title: Meera Bai Temple
meera.hero.desc: A sacred sanctuary dedicated to the mystic poet-saint Meera Bai and her eternal love for Lord Krishna.
meera.overview.p1: Meerabai, an ardent devotee of Lord Krishna’s, worshipped him at this temple. The structure is designed in the classic North Indian style of temples.
meera.architecture.p1: It rises from a raised plinth and its conical roof can be seen from far. The temple houses a beautiful shrine surrounded by an open porch with four small pavilions in four corners.
meera.references.title: References
light_show.hero.title: Light & Sound Show
light_show.hero.desc: A mesmerizing journey through the 1300-year history of Chittorgarh Fort, brought to life with state-of-the-art DMX LED lighting and 5.1 surround sound.
kirti.hero.title: Kirti Stambh
kirti.hero.desc: A magnificent 12th-century tower dedicated to the first Jain Tirthankara, Adinathji.
kirti.history.p1: This Tower of Fame is dedicated to Adinathji, the 1st Jain Tirthankara (great teacher). Built by a wealthy Jain merchant in the 12th century AD, it stands as a testament to the Jain community's contribution to Mewar's heritage.
kirti.architecture.p1: The seven-storied tower is adorned with intricate figures of the Digambars (Jain monks), showcasing the exquisite craftsmanship of the medieval era.
kirti.temples.p1: The tower is also located near the beautiful Jain temples of Neminath Ji, Adinath Ji, and Parshwanath Ji, forming a sacred complex within the fort.
light_show.overview.p1: Chittorgarh Fort Light & Sound Show is a traditional light & sound show featuring mesmerizing impacts of DMX controlled LED luminaries, gobo lights, 5.1 audio surround system. Show depicts history of the fort, its foundation, its rulers, wars & battles fought at the Fort, attack by Alauddin Khalji.. The show is now in operation.
light_show.experience.p1: The show offers a cinematic retelling of the fort's glorious past under the starlit sky. The combination of synchronized lights and powerful narration creates an unforgettable atmosphere, making it a must-visit experience for every traveler.
light_show.references.title: References
ratan_palace.hero.title: Ratan Singh Palace
ratan_palace.hero.desc: The winter palace of the royal family, it overlooks a small lake.
ratan_palace.overview.p1: The winter palace of the royal family, it overlooks a small lake.
ratan_palace.overview.p2: Although fairly rundown now, it is an interesting place to explore and attracts many tourists.
nagari.hero.title: Nagari
nagari.hero.desc: A historic village 18 Km North of Chittorgarh, Nagari was a flourishing ancient town known as Majhimika, rich in Hindu and Buddhist heritage.
nagari.overview.p1: Nagari, situated on the banks of river Berach, was known in the ancient era as Majhimika or Madhyamika. Inscriptions from 443 BC name this town as Majhimika, and it remained a flourishing center from the Mauryan period through the Gupta period.
nagari.overview.p2: Excavations at Nagari reveal a strong influence of both Hindu and Buddhist traditions. A large number of punch-marked and other ancient coins have been discovered, marking its importance as a commercial and cultural hub.
nagari.sibi.p1: In the first century, Nagari was ruled by the Sibi tribes. Coins found here bear the legend ‘majhamikaya sibi janapadasa’. The Sibi rule was eventually challenged by the Yavans (Greeks).
nagari.sibi.p2: Patanjali, the contemporary of Pushyamitra Sunga, mentions the Yavan attack on Madhyamika in 150 BC in his Mahabhashya. Later, Nagari came under the Western Kshatrapas in the 2nd century and the Malavas in the 3rd century, before the Huna conquest.
nagari.attractions.shiva.name: Ancient Shiva Temple
nagari.attractions.shiva.desc: A historic temple showing the deep-rooted religious significance of Nagari throughout the ages.
nagari.attractions.hathiyon.name: Hathiyon ka Bara
nagari.attractions.hathiyon.desc: An intriguing site associated with the historical layout of the ancient town.
nagari.attractions.prakash.name: Ubhdivat (Prakash Stambh)
nagari.attractions.prakash.desc: Also known as the Tower of Light, it stands as a testament to the town's ancient architectural brilliance.
nagari.references.title: Reference
attr.nagari.name: Nagari
attr.nagari.desc: An ancient archaeological site 18 Km from Chittorgarh, rich in Hindu and Buddhist history.
sitamata.hero.title: Sitamata Wildlife Sanctuary
sitamata.hero.desc: Spanning the Aravali and Vindhyachal ranges, Sitamata is a lush sanctuary famous for its unique teak forests and the rare flying squirrel.
sitamata.overview.p1: Spread over the meeting point of the Aravali and Vindhyachal ranges, Sitamata Wildlife Sanctuary is a biodiversity hotspot. It is uniquely known as the only forest in the region where valuable teak trees are found in abundance.
sitamata.overview.p2: The sanctuary is blessed with the flow of three rivers, with the Jakham and Karmoj being the most prominent, sustaining a rich ecosystem of flora and fauna.
sitamata.wildlife.flora.title: Unique Teak Forests
sitamata.wildlife.flora.desc: About 50% of the sanctuary is covered by teak trees, alongside species like Salar, Tendu, Amla, Bamboo, and Bel, making it a botanical paradise.
sitamata.wildlife.fauna.title: Diverse Wildlife
sitamata.wildlife.fauna.desc: The sanctuary is home to leopards, hyenas, jackals, foxes, jungle cats, porcupines, spotted deer, wild bears, four-horned antelopes, and nilgais.
sitamata.wildlife.squirrel.title: The Flying Squirrel
sitamata.wildlife.squirrel.desc: The most iconic inhabitant is the flying squirrel, which can be seen gliding between the trees during the night, a sight unique to Sitamata.
sitamata.references.title: References
bassi.hero.title: Bassi Wildlife Sanctuary
bassi.hero.desc: A sprawling sanctuary established in 1988, offering a rich tapestry of wetlands, mixed woodlands, and historic hunting towers.
bassi.overview.p1: Established in 1988 and situated just five kilometers from Bassi village, this sanctuary lies within the majestic Vindhyan hill range. Once the private hunting grounds of the rulers of Mewar, it now serves as a vital conservation area.
bassi.overview.p2: Visitors can still see the ancient and artistic 'Audhis' (hunting towers) scattered across the landscape, standing as silent witnesses to the region's royal past.
bassi.highlights.habitats.title: Diverse Ecosystems
bassi.highlights.habitats.desc: The sanctuary features a variety of habitats including lush wetlands, groves of mixed woodlands, and dense stands of Dhok and Khair trees.
bassi.highlights.fauna.title: Wild Encounters
bassi.highlights.fauna.desc: The area is home to diverse animals such as Chital, Sambar, Common Fox, Wild Boar, and the elusive Leopard.
bassi.highlights.birds.title: Avian Paradise
bassi.highlights.birds.desc: The Orai, Bassi, and Sarana dams are excellent sites for migratory and resident birds, most notably the graceful Sarus Crane.
bassi.references.title: Official References
attr.sitamata.name: Sitamata Sanctuary
attr.sitamata.desc: A lush sanctuary spread over Aravali and Vindhyachal ranges, home to the rare flying squirrel.

menal.hero.title: Menal Waterfall
menal.hero.desc: A beautiful 150-meter waterfall on the Bhilwara-Kota road, where the water falls into a V-shaped valley with great force.
menal.overview.p1: Located 80 kilometers from Bhilwara, on the Bhilwara-Kota road, is a beautiful waterfall where the water falls to a depth of 150 meters into a V-shaped valley with great force, making for a beautiful sight.
menal.overview.p2: People from all corners of the State flock to take it in. The best time to visit the Menal Waterfall is from July to October.
menal.references.title: Official Reference
sanwaliya.hero.title: Sanwaliya ji Dham
sanwaliya.hero.desc: A divine pilgrimage on the Chittorgarh-Udaipur Highway, where faith meets grandeur.
sanwaliya.history.p1: In the year 1840, based on a dream of a shepherd named Bholanath Gurjar, three identical idols of Lord Krishna (Sanwaliya ji) were found during excavation on the border of Bhadsauda-Bagund village.
sanwaliya.history.p2: These three idols were installed in three different locations: Prakatya Sthal (the discovery spot), Bhadsauda (the oldest temple), and Mandafiya (the grandest temple), creating a sacred triangle of devotion that draws millions of pilgrims annually.
sanwaliya.temple1.title: Prakatya Sthal
sanwaliya.temple1.desc: Located at the Bhadsauda-Bagund border, this is the exact spot where the idols were un-earthed from the ground.
sanwaliya.temple2.title: Bhadsauda (Oldest Temple)
sanwaliya.temple2.desc: The second idol was installed here, making it the oldest formal temple of Sanwaliya ji in the region.
sanwaliya.temple3.title: Mandafiya (Sanwaliya Dham)
sanwaliya.temple3.desc: The third and grandest temple, situated in Mandafiya, is known as Sanwaliya ji Dham and serves as the primary spiritual center.
sanwaliya.timings.title: Darshan & Arati Timings
